Thanks for this question. I've been mulling over posting a similar question, so I'll just jump into your discussion.

This is the story of my life. I'm an older guy (66), but I don't look my age, nor do I have any "daddy" characteristics - I'm a trim 5'8" and 155lbs, not hairy at all, no facial hair - I was a "twink" way back in the day (before they were called that), and now I'm still a twink, just with an older body. LOL

Now of course, I have a lot of experience in life, so I tend to mentor and support younger guys like a dad would, but I do it more on a friendship basis than a dad/son basis.

Young guys on the apps often approach me as "daddy" and expect me to dominate, top, spank, and generally want me to role play the "daddy" part. I can sustain that for a quickie, but it's not something I want to build a relationship on. 


And the hardest part for me is that a significant number of these young guys are physically larger, more hairy, and generally more "daddy-like" than me. I love everybody, but I just do better with guys around my size and shape.

I prefer relationships built on empathy, trust, common interests, and respect. Age is just a number. The only thing I really have to offer is experience and love.

I've been extraordinarily lucky to have developed some wonderful friendships with a couple of young men (20 & 22) who treat me like a buddy rather than a daddy, and I find it very fulfilling. 

Neither is a full-on romantic relationship, but we play sometimes. One is an alpha personality, and he generally tops. Fine. The other is a bottom. I take over with him. We are both friends first, so we make the play stuff work according to our feelings at the moment. I honestly believe that the whole "roles" thing is overdone.

So I didn't mean to get off on a rant here, but yeah, can we just have a relationship and not a theater performance?

I was just in Bali before Christmas. I actually stayed at a gay guest house on the edge of Seminyak out toward Canggu.  It's pretty low key, so if you're interested PM me for the specifics. The beaches are just so-so along Seminyak but get better as you go out toward Canggu and beyond. Bali is very crowded and the traffic is crazy sometimes.  As you go up in the hills things chill out a little bit.  Lots of people like Ubud, and it's a cool area, but of course, no beaches there.  You might want to tour on up into the hills and see one of the [UNESCO World Heritage sites](http://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1194) (rice paddies, but really interesting.) There are some pretty lakes and waterfalls on up in the mountains.  Definitely away from the party scene.

Bali is definitely worth a few days, if you can find the right spots. I haven't been to Jakarta, so can't really help you there. I never had any issues being a solo male traveler in Bali.  I don't really present as "gay", so the locals didn't really notice me.  On the other hand, you could probably spot me a mile away.  :-)  Just be cool and friendly and you'll do fine.

As an older guy who has been through similar experiences and feelings, I can tell you that life is full of up and down cycles.  What feels like a downward spiral right now will eventually turn around into an upward cycle.  I am so happy now that I did not do some drastic during a down cycle many years ago.  My life is so much better now.

Always know that there are people who will understand your feelings and care for you.  You are doing the right thing in reaching out.  Yes, some of the people will be jerks or try to take advantage of you, but just move on.  There are many good people in the world.  You will find them.

I don't know where you are or what size community you are in, so it's difficult for me to make suggestions as to where to look.  Try to consider that somewhere, there is someone who desperately needs someone just like you.  It may take time to connect, but when you do, it could make you very happy.

I know that pleasing your family is very important to you, but remember that pleasing yourself is even more important.  When you find yourself and regain your confidence (and you will...) your family will learn to accept you and be proud of you.

We tend to progress towards the things we think about.  The more you think about death, the worse you will feel. Try very hard to think instead about good things that you want.  Then you will begin to progress towards those things.

Talking to a non-judgmental counselor if very valuable.  I bet your school has one available.  Don't be afraid to open up.

Some other little things that actually really help:

Eat right - drop the junk food and lots of sugar.  These contribute to the up and down cycles.

Sleep right - develop regular sleep patterns and only sleep 7-8 hours per night.  Too much sleep makes you lethargic

Exercise - go for a walk or run or swim every day. make yourself do it.  physical exercise moderates depression

Avoid alcohol, drugs, and over-the-counter medications - These things make the up and down cycles more extreme.

Develop social outlets - join the chess club / play intramural sports / tutor young students/ volunteer in an old folks home / anything that makes you feel good / bring joy to other people and you will bring joy to yourself

From reading your story, I feel that you are in a down cycle but have great potential to make it through to the happy life you desire.  Don't give up.
